content: The life of money-making is a life of constraint, and wealth is clearly not the good we seek; for it is merely useful for the sake of something else.
author: Aristotle
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In Aristotle's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
